moves.why: Pulling is positive EV over stopping and all three open wells are identical Serpent wells, so no reason to prefer one; choose the middle arbitrarily.
Banking the guaranteed star is better than risking it on a ~30% void pull that would also hand a face-up star to the next seat; the unused reach is the price of safety.
One-groove rotation keeps my next reach at 3, and disc b +1 leaves a 4-well mixed sky (anvil, wheel, two serpents) rather than a 5-well flood; no single rotation can deny serpent entirely.
starting with an anvil pull: I have nothing yet and need breadth across constellations for nights; anvil is the one seat 0 has not touched
pull wheel first: if it succeeds I can take a serpent next and complete an all-three night, whose bonus outweighs the void risk; stopping now is safe but capped at 2
expected value favors the serpent pull: ~69% chance to complete a three-constellation night worth 8-9 versus safe 4, and the void risk is worth taking this early
rotating disc B back one closes both face-up stars at 3 and 6, leaving seat 2 only blind serpent wells to risk, and I need to deny easy points after busting
only concealed serpent wells are open; TAKE is unavailable, so a blind pull is the only way to gain, and single-pull EV is positive despite the ~1/4 void risk
